guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / major bleeding and shock
title: Embedded glass shard hand injury at a charity dance
setting: Charity dance. Catering team member tried to catch a falling glass, resulting in a large shard of glass embedded in palm, bleeding heavily.
verdictExplanation: Embedded glass shard in palm, bleeding heavily, pale, cold, clammy, and hypotensive (88/55). Sick: immediate bleed control and 999.

shared.response: Alert and responsive, in severe pain
shared.circulation: Skin is pale, cold, and clammy

history.history: Tried to catch a falling drinks glass, resulted in large shard embedded in palm 5 minutes ago
history.injuries: Shard of glass embedded in right palm, bleeding heavily
history.additional: Patient is in severe pain and highly panicked

followUp.question: What is the correct first aid management for this embedded glass shard?

options.text: Apply padding on either side of the glass to build up support, secure with a bandage, and do not remove the glass
Pull the glass shard out immediately to stop the pain and bleed
Apply a tourniquet above the elbow as a first-line treatment
Run to find the attacker to ensure scene safety before doing anything else

followUp.explanation: Never remove an embedded object. It acts as a plug to prevent severe bleeding. Build up padding on either side of the object to support it, secure with a bandage, and call 999. Tourniquets are only for uncontrolled catastrophic haemorrhage.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Do not remove the glass. Apply padding on either side, secure, call 999. Monitor for shock.
levelFlags.erNotes: Secure embedded object. Treat for hemorrhagic shock. Maintain pressure, administer oxygen, check BGL, and prepare for priority transport.
